pointers.sentence: Two changes of 6.2 alter how a request is served under ASGI, and both concern the one thread each ASGI request has, on which Django runs the synchronous code it calls with `thread_sensitive=True` (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.__call__`).
The notes' reasons are the cost of the switching and the database connections an error view uses (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

Since 6.2 every one built on the mixin with either hook has the flag false, and `BaseHandler.load_middleware` therefore runs them synchronously: together they make one call into the request's thread, and the centre of the chain, where the handler resolves the view and calls it, one call back to the loop (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.async_capable`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

Since 6.2 every one built on the mixin with either hook has the flag false, and `BaseHandler.load_middleware` therefore runs them synchronously: together they make one call into the request's thread, and the centre of the chain, where the handler resolves the view and calls it, one call back to the loop (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.async_capable`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).
Since 6.2 the chain is one call, and only `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view` is still handed over on its own, as the view is (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response_async`).

`LoginRequiredMiddleware` and `XViewMiddleware`, which have only a `process_view`, keep the mixin's flag, still true (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.async_capable`), and `RemoteUserMiddleware`, not built on the mixin, declares it true (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware`).

`LoginRequiredMiddleware` and `XViewMiddleware`, which have only a `process_view`, keep the mixin's flag, still true (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.async_capable`), and `RemoteUserMiddleware`, not built on the mixin, declares it true (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:RemoteUserMiddleware`).

A project's own class built directly on the mixin keeps the flag true unless it sets it, and so takes the mode of the layer inside it, the next in `MIDDLEWARE`: after all of Django's synchronous ones it runs in async mode as before, and directly before one it now runs synchronously, in their one call (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

`MiddlewareMixin` itself moved in 6.2, from `django.utils.deprecation` to `django.middleware`; the old import still works, and warns with `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`; [What changed](../changes.md#an-old-habit-release-by-release)).

Before 6.2 that ran on a shared pool of threads, the notes say; since 6.2 the call passes `thread_sensitive=True`, which sends it to the request's own thread (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`).

A connection belongs to the thread that opened it (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionHandler.thread_critical`), and `close_old_connections`, which closes one that is broken or past its age, runs on the request's thread as the request starts and ends (`django/db/__init__.py:close_old_connections`); before 6.2 it could not reach a connection that a `handler404` or a `handler500` opened on a pool thread.

Since 5.0 an `"http.disconnect"` that arrives before the response is made cancels the work, so that a view can clean up (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`).

A coroutine view is cancelled where it awaits, while synchronous code already running on the request's thread runs to its end (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.handle`; [The two entry points](../handlers/entry.md#an-asgi-request)).

Since 6.0 the `"cookie"` headers are joined with a semicolon and a space into `"HTTP_COOKIE"`, where any other repeated header is joined with commas (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`), and the cookie parser, which splits on semicolons alone, finds both (`django/http/cookie.py:parse_cookie`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).

Django's view decorators did not support coroutine views before 5.0, the notes say (`docs/releases/5.0.txt`).

Since then each decorator in `django/views/decorators/` but `sensitive_variables`, and each made from a middleware, chooses between a `def` wrapper and an `async def` one that awaits the view (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`, `django/utils/decorators.py:make_middleware_decorator`); `sensitive_variables` records which of a coroutine function's variables are sensitive without wrapping it (`django/views/decorators/debug.py:sensitive_variables`).

Since 5.2 `method_decorator` marks its replacement as a coroutine function when the method is one (`django/utils/decorators.py:_multi_decorate`; [Asynchronous views](../views/async.md#what-a-decorator-has-to-keep)).
The guard was against an attack on a JSON array through JavaScript's array prototype, which, the 6.2 notes say, ECMAScript 5 closed (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
Since 6.2 the default is `None`, read as false, so a list is serialised (`django/http/response.py:JsonResponse.__init__`).
Before 6.1 the parser decoded it leniently: invalid data "could be silently ignored or result in empty values", the 6.1 notes say (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Since 6.1 `MultiPartParser.parse` decodes with `validate=True`, which refuses any character outside the Base64 alphabet (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.parse`; [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md)).

Nothing warns or fails: from 6.1 a field whose Base64 is written in lines, as MIME writes it, arrives undecoded, while the same data in a file still decodes (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.parse`).

| `RedirectView.preserve_request` | new, given to the response the view makes | 6.1 | `django/views/generic/base.py:RedirectView.get` |

| a redirect's maximum length | a keyword-only max_length, also taken by `redirect`: `MAX_URL_REDIRECT_LENGTH` unless given, `None` for no check; the limit now measures the escaped `"Location"` | 6.1 | `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__` |
| get_converter | removed; the registry is read through `get_converters` | 5.1 | `django/urls/converters.py:get_converters` |
